moc_star.text: the MOC* for these tests was defined as the maximum oxygen concentration at which the flame was observed to self-extinguish during the drop time

ulois_star.text: The ULOI* criterion was minimum oxygen concentration where the flame survived the full drop time

criteria_differ.text: It should be noted that the low g extinction limit criteria are not the same as 1g due to time constraints in drop testing

martian_rpm.text: To achieve Martian gravity levels, the rotation rate required is 30.8 RPM

base.text: Total base spread of ~6cm until extinction.

points.outcome: Lunar-g buoyant extinction at substantially HIGHER O2 than the WSTF data (less flammable at lunar g than predicted from 1 g forced flow). Numeric O2 values are plot only, not extracted here.

p.text: the planned NASA lunar habitat pressure of 56.5 kPa (8.2 psia)

points.sample: 2 cm wide (Fig 1) and 1 cm wide (inset)
points.outcome: Upward spread rate varied linearly with gravity; downward spread rate non-monotonic with a peak near 0.38 g. Flammability boundaries and spread rates are plot only, not extracted here.

cond.text: Test pressures between 0.2-0.4 atmospheres were established using primary standard, precision mixtures of 21% O2

fuel.text: Fuel samples were a thin cellulosic tissue, trade name

peak.text: The downward spread rate is non- monotonic and peaks near the Martian gravity levels of 0.38 g/gEarth

lin.text: The upward burning spread rate varied linearly with gravity level for all pressure environments and sample widths tested

fig1.text: burned in 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia) air at various gravity levels

notes: Thin tissue in reduced-pressure air, not a spacecraft-material limit test.

rejected_or_plot_only.why: Lunar-g and WSTF O2 limits are plotted, not tabulated or stated in text (plot only, not extracted); only Table 2 deltas exist, already in data/lunar_g/.
Flammability boundaries and spread rates versus g are plotted (Figs 1, 2, 6, 7); only conditions and qualitative trends are stated in text.

State that partial-g flames propagated at the normal-g MOC and that lunar-g MOC can be lower than 0 g or Martian g for Nomex, Mylar, Ultem, but give no numbers; the numbers are in Olson 2012 Table I (NTRS 20130010991).
Describe the Sacksteder/T'ien KC-135 downward-spread maximum near Martian g and the U-shaped boundary; O2 boundary values are in a plot, text is qualitative.
An expectation for planning FM2 hardware, not a measurement; the FM2 chamber plans (37/33/29/25% O2 at 8.2 psia) are test plans, not data.
